title: From your remote to the server and back

sentences.speaker: spk_0
sentences.text: You press play on your TV remote. Here's what happens in the next second.

sentences.speaker: spk_0
sentences.text: First, the app needs an address. It asks a DNS server to turn a name like video dot example dot com into an IP address, usually in well under a tenth of a second.

sentences.speaker: spk_0
sentences.text: Then it opens a secure connection, HTTPS, so nobody along the way can read or change what's sent.

sentences.speaker: spk_0
sentences.text: The request leaves through your Wi-Fi router to your internet provider.

sentences.speaker: spk_0
sentences.text: From there it doesn't travel to some faraway data centre. It goes to a nearby edge server of a content delivery network.

sentences.speaker: spk_0
sentences.text: If the edge already has the video cached, it answers straight away. If not, it fetches it once from the origin server and keeps a copy for the next viewer.

sentences.speaker: spk_0
sentences.text: The video comes back in small chunks of a few seconds each, and the player keeps asking for the next one, picking a lower quality if your connection slows.

sentences.speaker: spk_0
sentences.text: That round trip, every few seconds, is why the picture starts fast and keeps going.

note: Example transcript written by StudioX to show the pipeline on other genres; not a real episode.
